title: Understanding the Counsellor Salary: Hourly Rates, Annual Pay, and Award Coverage
description: Learn how to convert a counsellor salary from hourly to annual, including award rates, casual loading, tax, and super. Based on ABS and Fair Work data.
salarySummary: The median full-time counsellor salary is about $1,477 per week, or roughly $39 per hour, based on ABS data, assuming a 38-hour week.

faqs.q: What is the average counsellor salary in Australia?
faqs.a: According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) Survey of Employee Earnings and Hours (May 2023), the median full-time weekly earnings for counsellors are $1,477, and the median hourly earnings are $39. This is below the all-occupations median of $1,697 per week. Note that these figures are for non-managerial full-time employees and exclude overtime. Actual pay can vary by industry, experience, and whether you are covered by an award or enterprise agreement.

faqs.q: How is casual loading applied to a counsellor salary?
faqs.a: Casual employees covered by an award are entitled to a casual loading, typically 25% on top of the minimum hourly rate. For example, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour for permanent employees; casuals receive $33.05 per hour including the 25% loading. If you are a casual counsellor, your base hourly rate should be the award rate plus the loading. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading into a calculator – use the base rate and check the casual loading box separately.

faqs.q: What award covers counsellors, and how do I find the correct pay rate?
faqs.a: Counsellors may be covered by the Health Professionals and Support Services Award [MA000027] or the Social, Community, Home Care and Disability Services Industry Award [MA000100] (SCHADS Award), depending on their employer and role. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides pay guides for these awards with minimum rates, allowances, and penalty rates. You can access them via the pay guides page on the Fair Work Ombudsman website. Always check the specific award classification that matches your job duties.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Counsellor Salary

If you are a counsellor or considering a career in counselling, knowing how to convert your hourly rate to an annual salary is essential for budgeting, negotiating, and comparing job offers. This article explains the key figures for a **counsellor salary** in Australia, including award rates, median earnings, casual loading, tax, and superannuation.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly to Annual

The standard formula to estimate annual gross pay is:

**Annual salary ≈ hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

Most full-time roles in Australia are based on a 38-hour week, as set by the National Employment Standards. When no other hours are specified, we assume 38 hours. For example, if your hourly rate is $39, the calculation is:

$39 × 38 × 52 = $77,064 per year

You can also calculate your fortnightly pay: weekly pay × 2. For a $39/hour rate, weekly pay is $1,482 (39 × 38), so fortnightly is $2,964.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates vs Median Earnings

It is important to distinguish between three different pay references:

- **National Minimum Wage**: From 1 July 2026, the minimum is $26.44 per hour for permanent employees, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive $33.05 per hour including 25% loading.
- **Award Rates**: Many counsellors are covered by modern awards such as the Health Professionals and Support Services Award or the SCHADS Award. These set minimum pay rates higher than the National Minimum Wage. The Fair Work Commission publishes the Modern Awards Pay Database with detailed classification rates.
- **Median Earnings**: The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) reports that the median full-time counsellor earns $1,477 per week (before tax), or about $39 per hour. This is a useful benchmark but may not reflect your specific situation.

When these sources conflict, always prefer the Fair Work Ombudsman, Fair Work Commission, ABS, and Australian Taxation Office over recruiter surveys.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

If you work as a casual counsellor, you are entitled to a casual loading – typically 25% on top of the minimum award rate. This compensates for lack of paid leave. When using a pay calculator, enter your base hourly rate (without loading) and check the casual loading box. Do not enter a rate that already includes the loading.

Superannuation (super) is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For example, on a $77,064 annual salary, your employer would contribute an additional $9,247.68 per year into your super fund.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your take-home pay depends on tax brackets and the Medicare levy. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:

- Nil on income up to $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (with possible reductions for low-income earners). For a counsellor earning $77,064, the estimated tax would be approximately $14,667 plus Medicare, leaving a take-home pay of around $60,000 per year, before any salary sacrifice or deductions.

### Using the Timesheet and Pay Guides

To calculate your own figures, use [the timesheet](/). It allows you to enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading. The tool will show your weekly, fortnightly, monthly, and annual gross pay, along with estimated tax and super.

For award-specific rates, refer to the [pay guides](/blog) provided by the Fair Work Ombudsman. These guides list minimum pay rates, allowances, and penalty rates for each classification under your award.

### Important Disclaimer

The annual pay shown here is an estimate based on hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

### Summary

A counsellor salary in Australia can range from award minimums to above-median levels depending on experience and employer. Use the formula hourly × 38 × 52 to estimate annual pay, check your award via Fair Work Ombudsman pay guides, and remember that super and casual loading are paid on top. For a personalised calculation, visit [the timesheet](/).
